definition_zh: 粗鲁的；粗野无礼的；缺乏教养的
core_image: 宴席上大张着嘴剔牙的宾客
scene: 宴席间他高声打断每个人，还伸手抓过最后一块蛋糕。His boorish behaviour embarrassed the whole table.
sceneCN: 这里 boorish 是「粗鲁的」（第 1 个义项：举止粗野、不体谅人）；句意是他粗鲁的举止让整桌人都难堪。

derivatives.zh: 词根名词，义为「粗人；乡下佬」

senses.title: Rude in social behaviour
senses.definition: offending others by crude, insensitive manners
senses.definitionCN: 以粗野、不体贴的举止冒犯他人
senses.example: His boorish behaviour embarrassed the whole table.
senses.exampleCN: 他粗鲁的举止让整桌人都难堪。
senses.why: Old būr was a countryman; town etiquette called the unrefined peasant-like.
senses.whyCN: 古义 būr 指农人，城市礼俗便以「乡气」讥粗野无文。

senses.title: Insensitive to others' comfort
senses.definition: blind or indifferent to other people's feelings and comfort
senses.definitionCN: 对他人感受与舒适漠然不觉
senses.example: It was boorish to keep talking while she wept.
senses.exampleCN: 她落泪时他还滔滔不绝，实在粗鲁。
senses.why: The boor notices no one but his own appetite.
senses.whyCN: 粗人只看见自己的胃口，看不见别人。

senses.title: Coarse in speech and jokes
senses.definition: vulgar or crude in language and humour
senses.example: His boorish jokes killed the dinner conversation.
senses.exampleCN: 他的粗俗玩笑让餐桌上的交谈哑了火。
senses.why: Refinement was measured at table; coarseness there was the type of the boor.
senses.whyCN: 教养以餐桌为尺，桌上的粗鄙正是粗人的写照。

senses.title: Loud and unmannered in public
senses.definition: behaving loudly and without public manners
senses.example: Boorish tourists shouted through the quiet cathedral.
senses.exampleCN: 粗鲁的游客在安静的教堂里大呼小叫。
senses.why: Public space demands restraint the boor never learned.
senses.whyCN: 公共空间要求约束，而粗人从未学过。

senses.title: Greedy or self-centred at table
senses.definition: showing bad table manners or appetite without regard for others
senses.definitionCN: 吃相不顾他人、毫无餐桌礼数
senses.example: He reached across three plates in a boorish grab.
senses.exampleCN: 他伸手越过三个盘子粗鲁地抓菜。
senses.why: The original peasant fed body first; etiquette reversed the order.
senses.whyCN: 古之农人先饱口腹，礼俗则将次序倒转。

senses.title: Aggressive and domineering
senses.definition: using rudeness as force to push others aside
senses.definitionCN: 以粗鲁为手段压制他人
senses.example: Her boorish interruptions silenced the junior staff.
senses.exampleCN: 她蛮横的插话让资浅员工噤声。
senses.why: Rudeness is the boor's only known tool of power.
senses.whyCN: 粗鲁是粗人唯一懂得的权力工具。

senses.title: Uncultivated in taste
senses.definitionCN: 显示出文化修养的欠缺
senses.example: He called the opera boring with boorish frankness.
senses.exampleCN: 他以粗野的直白宣称歌剧无聊透顶。
senses.why: The country-court divide of old English society lives in the word.
senses.whyCN: 古英语社会中乡村与宫廷的对立仍活在这词里。

senses.title: Cloddish in friendship
senses.definition: failing friends through heavy, unthinking behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 因愚钝粗率而怠慢朋友
senses.example: Boorish as ever, he forgot her birthday twice.
senses.exampleCN: 他一如既往地粗率，两次忘了她的生日。
senses.why: Sensitivity is the polishing the boor's rough nature lacks.
senses.whyCN: 体贴正是粗坯之性所缺的那道打磨。

intro.en: Boorish grows from boor, from Old English bur, a farmer or dweller.
intro.cn: boorish 由 boor 而来，boor 出自古英语 bur「农人、居者」。

items.en: a root of dwelling, also behind bower and build.
items.cn: 词根表「居所」，bower、build 亦属同族。

items.en: bur or gebur meant farmer, countryman.
items.cn: 古英语 bur／gebur 意为「农人、乡下人」。

items.en: boor named the peasant, with no contempt at first.
items.cn: 中古英语 boor 指农人，初无贬义。

items.en: courtly society gave boor its shade of coarse manners; boorish followed.
items.cn: 16 世纪宫廷社会赋予 boor「粗野」之贬义，boorish 随之而来。

items.en: now means any rude, insensitive person or manner, urban or rural.
items.cn: 今泛指粗鲁不体贴之人或举止，无论城乡。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the boor root; the near-meaning group gathers rude words.
note.cn: 形近组共享 boor 词根；近义组收粗鲁类词。

entries.definitionCN: 乏味的——拼写相近，词源不同
乖戾无礼的——同为农夫贬义词
粗笨无礼的——偏肢体笨拙

normalIntro.en: Boorish is the manners of a boor, the old word for peasant.
normalIntro.cn: boorish 即 boor（古义农人）的做派。

normal.en: Rhymes it with poor-ish to recall the sense.
normal.cn: 与 poor-ish 押韵帮助记忆。

abstract.en: See a guest talking with his mouth full, pointing with his fork.
abstract.cn: 看满嘴食物还用叉子指人的宾客。

abstract.en: Hear a phone blaring comedy clips in a funeral hall.
abstract.cn: 听葬礼大厅里外放搞笑视频的手机。

abstract.en: Feel someone stepping on your heels without a glance back.
abstract.cn: 感受被人踩了鞋跟却连头都不回。

examples.en: His boorish behaviour embarrassed the whole table.
examples.cn: 他粗鲁的举止让整桌人都难堪。

examples.en: Boorish tourists shouted through the quiet cathedral.
examples.cn: 粗鲁的游客在安静的教堂里大呼小叫。

examples.en: Her boorish interruptions silenced the junior staff.
examples.cn: 她蛮横的插话让资浅员工噤声。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「不耳食」——粗人饭桌上「不耳」旁人之言、只顾自食，粗鲁无礼。

root: 古英语 bur／gebur「农人、居者」（日耳曼词根表「居所」，与 bower、build 同源）；中古英语 boor 本指农人，16 世纪在宫廷礼俗语境中获得「粗野」贬义，boorish「粗鲁的」随之定型。

sensesIntro.en: From the farmer at the court's edge to any guest who ruins the table, boorish measures manners against refinement.
sensesIntro.cn: 从宫廷边缘的农人到搅局席间的宾客，boorish 始终以教养为尺量度举止。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a guest cleaning his teeth at the open mouth
core.cn: 核心意象：席间张口剔牙的宾客

branches.cn: 粗鲁的行止、言语与喧哗

intro.en: The -ish suffix turns the boor into a manner.
intro.cn: -ish 后缀把「粗人」化为一种做派。

latinIntro.cn: 日耳曼词根，无拉丁同族词。

items.meaning: a rude person; farmer of old
